_description: old-world lore beats surfaced on any search of an ambient noun. Each entry is a one-line observation written generically enough that {noun} substitution feels natural across most scene props (a chain, a wall, a wagon, a console, the silt itself). Surfaces at a 25% rate inside narrateAmbientFind, layered alongside the rarer hidden-text reveal for genuine writing surfaces. Tone: Verbal's voice — observational, hint-loaded, never lecture.
lines: The {noun} carries the same blue-mud crust every relic-age artifact wears down here. Six inches of silt accreted since the flood last raised the seas.
You catch the faint hum the old-world energy leaves on every surface it has touched longer than a season. The {noun} hums.
An old scavenger trick: tilt the {noun} into low light and see if the etch-marks show. scavengers etch everything they recover.
The mud-glass around the {noun} is fractured in the radial pattern a slow arcane pressure produces. The flood didn't cool evenly.
Whoever last touched the {noun} left a black-cloak fiber under it. The Monarch's people travel here in pairs, never alone.
The Order's sigil — three concentric rings — is half-worn into the {noun}'s underside. Some scribe sanctified this and then someone else used it as a tool.
the order doctrine says a {noun} like this is a temple-offering, fallen from the Red Tower's first ring. Doctrine says many things.
The grain on the {noun} runs against itself in two directions — pre-flood manufacture, machined by something that had patience and a hardness this world no longer makes.
A drift of arcane Dust has settled into the {noun}'s seams. The dust is a relic in itself — pre-flood air, sealed.
deep folk would salvage this. old-world Giants would crush it. scavengers would tag it for return. Each faction reads the {noun} differently.
The old-world Giants used {noun}-shaped tokens to mark passage of high seasons. The mark has been gone from the cycle for centuries.
The {noun}'s edge is gnawed where a Mud Spider tested it for prey. Two of them, working in turn, by the bite-pattern.
Smoke-stain on the {noun} is darker on the leeward side. Whoever burned this fire kept watch on the windward.
A pre-flood factory in Drakova made things this shape, before the buried city was buried. The catalog number runs along the seam if it survived.
The scavengers call them 'glass scars' — the white discoloration around the {noun} where mud-glass crystallized fast. The flood was hotter here.
Iron Spear tribes used to spike {noun}s like this into the ground as territorial markers. They are not a tribe anymore.
energy Undead leave a particular cold on objects they have touched. The {noun} is not cold. Whatever you fear, it's not that.
If you held the {noun} during a Whisper Fog, it would carry voices. The Order pays well for objects that hold voices.
The construction is too clean to be old-world and too crude to be Drakovan. The dispossessed Cradle of Dusk made things in this style for one generation.
energyborn artisans worked with {noun}-shaped templates — the curve isn't an accident. It catches the energy the way a lens catches light.
Whoever set up this scene was a scavenger. The angle of the {noun} matches their salvage-survey protocol: 14 degrees off cardinal north.
The Mud Seas surface debris like this in the wet season. Whatever was carrying the {noun} is on the bottom of the Seas now.
True old-worlds scratch a single mark into objects they recover from the buried country. There's a mark on the {noun}. Someone has already passed through.
A relic this old, this exposed, should have crumbled. The energy stone matrix in the {noun} is holding it together. energy stone holds many things together.
The flood didn't drown this world all at once. The {noun}'s wear-pattern says it sat under shallow water for a generation before the mud took it.
scavengers tell new initiates: 'If you find a {noun} that fits in your hand and isn't broken, sell it. If you find one that's broken, learn from it.'
Frost-line on the {noun} runs at exactly the level of the local arcane pressure — chest-high here, knee-high in the Buried Cities, gone in the Outskirts proper.
old-world Giants left their marks in palmprints rather than glyphs — their hands were bigger than the writing surface most relics offered. The {noun} has no palmprint.
Servants of the Giants comb the Outskirts for {noun}-shaped tribute. Whatever you do with this, don't leave it where they walk.
The Cradle of Dusk's wreck-field is upwind. Days when the wind shifts, debris like the {noun} ends up in the Outskirts.
A old-world inscription read: 'The buried country keeps what it is given.' Whoever left the {noun} here gave it to the buried country.
The energy grid that lit this world still pulses, weak. The {noun} sits exactly on a node. The pulse is what you've been hearing without naming.
Black-cloak agents prefer relics that don't draw attention. The {noun} is unremarkable enough that they'd take it without asking who you are.
The the order recovers {noun}s like this and places them at the Red Tower's base. The Red Tower has 47 visible rings. It had more, once.
arcane Mutation residue clings to objects that have been near a wraith for too long. The {noun} has the residue. The wraith may still be near.
Old Drakova exported {noun}-shaped tokens as currency before the wars. They are not currency now. They are sometimes still tokens.
The old-world moons were two before the flood and one after. The {noun}'s shadow falls strangely some nights for reasons not yet explained.
scavenger code for the {noun}: salvage if portable, mark if not. Someone marked this with a careful chalk-X. The chalk has not yet washed away.
